name: CROSS
canonical: a tall rough-hewn unfinished wooden Roman execution cross, two heavy hand-split timbers fixed in a plain T or Latin shape, the upright planted into the ground and the crossbeam lashed and pegged across it, bark-flecked and splintered, weathered grey-brown. A first-century instrument of death — NOT a smooth polished modern crucifix, NOT a gilded or jewelled church cross, NOT a thin geometric symbol; no figure of Christ on it (bare cross)
notes: Pass `anchor` as --image to lock identity/world across scenes.
